overview: Resolute Mining is an ASX/LSE-listed, Africa-focused gold producer operating the Syama underground/open-pit mine in Mali and the Mako open-pit mine in Senegal, with a third growth pillar under construction at the Doropo project in Côte d'Ivoire (acquired May 2025) targeting first gold in H1 2028. The company aims to lift group production to a 500,000 oz/year run-rate by the end of 2028 by combining Syama's Sulphide Conversion Project, a Mako life-extension, and Doropo's development. Resolute has a troubled recent history with the Malian government, including the 2024 detention of its then-CEO and colleagues and a $159.9 million settlement, which continues to weigh on investor perception of jurisdictional risk even as 2025-2026 gold prices have been at record highs.

business_model.summary: Resolute is a single-commodity (gold) producer that generates nearly all revenue from mined and refined gold sold at spot/near-spot prices into the international bullion market. There is no recurring/subscription revenue; income is entirely transactional and highly leveraged to realized gold price, ore grade, throughput and all-in sustaining costs (AISC). Growth is funded from operating cash flow plus project-level local bank financing (e.g., Doropo's local financing facility) rather than a diversified sales mix.

revenue_streams.name: Syama (Mali) gold sales
revenue_streams.trend: declining in 2026 (guidance cut) but historically the largest contributor

revenue_streams.name: Mako (Senegal) gold sales
revenue_streams.trend: declining as mine transitions from open-pit to stockpile processing only

revenue_streams.name: Doropo (Côte d'Ivoire)
revenue_streams.trend: under construction, first gold expected H1 2028

business_model.customer_type: B2B/commodity - gold sold to bullion banks/refiners at prevailing market prices; no customer concentration risk in the traditional sense since gold is a fungible commodity
business_model.geographic_mix: Mali (Syama, ~majority of production and reserves), Senegal (Mako), Côte d'Ivoire (Doropo/ABC/La Debo development, ~40% of combined Mineral Resources in-country), residual exploration exposure in Guinea; corporate domicile Australia, dual-listed ASX/LSE

competitive_position.market_position: Mid-tier West African gold producer (~280koz produced in FY2025, guided materially lower in FY2026) with a large (17.6 Moz) resource base relative to its market cap, but well below the scale of majors like Barrick or AngloGold Ashanti in the same jurisdictions

moat_factors.description: 17.6 Moz global Mineral Resource (2025) including Syama's underground sulphide ore body gives multi-decade mine life optionality and a pipeline of satellite/exploration targets across four West African countries
Decades of operating history in Mali and Senegal give sunk infrastructure and permitting advantages over new entrants, though this cuts both ways given regulatory entanglement

Having settled with Mali and secured Doropo's mining permit in Côte d'Ivoire, management argues stakeholder relationships have been rebuilt, but this is fragile and event-driven rather than structural

Group AISC of ~$1,843/oz in FY2025 rising toward $2,250-2,350/oz guided for FY2026 is high versus many peers; Resolute is not a low-cost producer, so its competitive advantage rests on resource scale and gold price leverage rather than a cost moat

weaknesses: No durable cost advantage - AISC has risen sharply and sits at the higher end of the sector in FY2026 guidance
Heavy single-asset concentration in Syama, which alone drives the majority of group production and cash flow
Operates exclusively in jurisdictions (Mali, Guinea, increasingly broader Sahel) with elevated sovereign, security and regulatory risk versus peers with more diversified geographic footprints
History of adversarial relations with host governments (Mali 2024 crisis; Guinea permit revocations in 2025) undermines the reliability of its resource-to-reserve conversion and cost outlook
Small-to-mid cap scale limits access to capital compared to major diversified gold producers

growth_drivers: Doropo development in Côte d'Ivoire - construction underway following FID and mining permit grant, targeting first gold H1 2028, ~13-year initial mine life, diversifies the portfolio into a lower-risk jurisdiction

Syama Sulphide Conversion Project (SSCP) - expanding sulphide processing capacity from 2.4Mtpa to 4Mtpa, targeted completion Q2 2026 and ramp-up Q3 2026, intended to improve recoveries and unit costs once operational disruptions ease
Mako Life Extension Project - studies underway to extend mine life beyond current stockpile-processing phase via new licence applications and satellite deposits (Tomboronkoto)
ABC Project resource growth in Côte d'Ivoire - Inferred Mineral Resource upgraded to ~3.0 Moz (July 2026), adding to a combined ~7.2 Moz Managed Mineral Resource base in-country (~40% of group total)
Stated target of 500,000 oz/year group production run-rate by end of 2028
Exploration across four West African countries (Mali, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea) with ongoing drilling campaigns
Strong balance sheet (net cash of $317.4 million at 30 June 2026) funding growth capex without heavy reliance on new equity or debt
Secular tailwind: record and rising gold prices in 2026 (spot above $4,000-5,500/oz through the year) materially expanding realized margins even amid production shortfalls

business.description: Syama alone was guided to produce 150,000-160,000 oz of the FY2026 group total after a September 2026 downgrade, meaning operational disruption at a single mine can move group results materially

Q2-Q3 2026 saw production fall sharply (Q2 gold poured of ~45,192 oz vs 151,460 oz a year earlier) due to security-related road insecurity delaying equipment delivery to the A21 open pit and intermittent explosives supply during the wet season
Mako has transitioned from open-pit mining to processing lower-grade stockpiles only, structurally shrinking output from that asset absent a life-extension approval

Construction is capital-intensive (guided $310-360 million current-cycle capex, dominated by Doropo) with $105 million of local bank financing still to be finalized in Q3 2026; delays or cost overruns would pressure the balance sheet and delay the diversification benefit
Resolute's exploration permits in Guinea were reportedly swept up in a nationwide government revocation of 100+ permits in 2025; formal resolution remains pending

financial.description: Group AISC guidance has risen from $1,650-1,750/oz (initial 2025 guidance) to $2,250-2,350/oz for FY2026, driven by higher royalties (a function of higher gold prices) and lower production absorbing fixed costs, compressing margin even as revenue benefits from price
Diesel, explosives and imported mining equipment costs in landlocked/logistics-constrained Mali are exposed to both FX and supply-chain disruption

Resolute retains deferred consideration from the divested Ravenswood (Australia) mine - a Vendor Financing Promissory Note (~A$68m) and an Upside Sharing Promissory Note (up to A$150m) - both counterparty-dependent and of uncertain ultimate recovery after the 2025 termination of Ravenswood's sale process

regulatory.description: Following the 2024 Protocol and $159.9 million settlement, Syama moved onto the new Mining Code, which management estimates adds ~US$250/oz of additional production costs; full implementation terms with the Malian state remained unresolved as of the FY2025 report despite a target 90-day negotiation window

Mali's military-led government has aggressively pursued foreign miners for increased tax/royalty take (Resolute's CEO and colleagues were detained in Nov 2024; Barrick Gold executives were separately detained and charged over its Loulo-Gounkoto complex), reflecting a sector-wide, not company-specific, jurisdictional risk across the Sahel
The Guinea permit revocations demonstrate that regulatory risk extends beyond Mali to other operating jurisdictions in the region

macro.description: Nearly 100% of revenue is gold-price-linked; while 2025-2026 has seen record prices (spot above $5,500/oz intraday in January 2026, dipping below $4,000/oz in June 2026), a sustained pullback would hit revenue and cash flow directly with no diversification buffer
Deteriorating security in Mali directly disrupted logistics/explosives supply chains in 2026, and continued instability could further impair operations or safety

Low direct rate sensitivity given a net cash balance sheet ($317.4 million at 30 June 2026), but reserve/resource economics and cost inflation are still moderately exposed to broader macro conditions in-country

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Gold mining sector outlook is currently very favorable on price: gold reached record highs above $5,500/oz intraday in January 2026 and major banks (JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley) have raised 2026-2027 targets toward $5,000-6,000/oz driven by central bank buying (700-900 tonnes/year), de-dollarization, and geopolitical hedging demand. This macro tailwind is currently offsetting Resolute's company-specific operational and jurisdictional setbacks.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - gold mining margins are strongly cyclical with the gold price; Resolute's cost structure (rising AISC) adds operating leverage in both directions
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity given net cash position; indirect sensitivity via gold's inverse relationship to real interest rates and the US dollar
key_input_costs: Mining equipment and spare parts (import-dependent, logistics-constrained in landlocked Mali)
Government royalties (rise mechanically with gold price)

recent_developments.event: Resolute cut FY2026 group production guidance to 205,000-225,000 oz (from 250,000-275,000 oz) at AISC of $2,250-2,350/oz (from $2,000-2,200/oz), driven by a Syama-specific cut to 150,000-160,000 oz at $2,300-2,400/oz AISC; shares fell as much as 8.5% to around A$1.24, erasing much of the year's gains

H1 2026 results: revenue of $584.7 million (gold sales of 123,951 oz at average realized price of $4,712/oz), EBITDA of $323.9 million (+41.5% YoY), net profit after tax of $162.6 million, and net cash surged to $317.4 million (+189% YoY) even as gold production fell to 104,795 oz from 151,460 oz in H1 2025

ABC Project (Côte d'Ivoire) Inferred Mineral Resource upgraded to 133 Mt at 0.71 g/t Au for ~3.0 Moz contained gold, reinforcing the Côte d'Ivoire growth pipeline (combined ~7.2 Moz managed Mineral Resources, ~40% of group total)

Q2 2026 unaudited production results showed a sharp production slump to 45,192 oz group-wide (from 151,460 oz in H1 2025 combined periods), with Syama output around 30,000 oz versus a 40,000-45,000 oz target, driven by security-related logistics disruptions and explosives shortages in Mali during the wet season

Resolute supported/participated in the Chengtun Gold Ontario acquisition of Loncor Gold Inc. (a DRC-focused explorer in which Resolute held an ~18% stake), realizing approximately US$31 million for its shares, expected to close around Q1 2026, bolstering Resolute's financial position

Completed the acquisition of the Doropo (and ABC) gold development projects in Côte d'Ivoire from AngloGold Ashanti, adding a third West African operating jurisdiction and a stated pathway to a 500,000 oz/year group production run-rate by end-2028

Doropo Mining Permit granted; project advanced through Final Investment Decision (FID) and into construction during Q2 2026, with initial gold production targeted for H1 2028 and an approximately 13-year mine life

Guinea exploration permits (Niagassola, Doko, Siguiri-Kouroussa) reportedly swept into a nationwide revocation of 100+ mining permits by the Guinean government; resolution remained pending as of mid-2025 disclosures

Mali crisis: then-CEO Terence Holohan and two colleagues detained in Bamako (Nov 2024) amid a dispute over alleged back taxes; released after Resolute signed a Protocol with the Government of Mali and made $159.9 million in settlement payments (final payment 31 Dec 2024), with Syama moved onto the 2023 Mining Code (adding an estimated ~US$250/oz to production costs)
CEO Terry Holohan departed the company; Chris Eger appointed CEO, Dave Jackson CFO, and (from July 2025) Gavin Harris COO, completing a full senior leadership transition following the 2024 crisis

Cut from 195,000-210,000 oz due to security-related logistics disruptions, explosives supply constraints and slower open-pit equipment mobilization at A21

items.notes: Includes Doropo construction; $105 million of local bank financing still to be finalized in Q3 2026 to sustain construction momentum
Approximately 13-year initial mine life; construction moved from FID into active execution in Q2 2026
Combines Syama SSCP ramp-up, Mako life extension, and Doropo first production

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Chris Eger acknowledged that 'the challenging operating environment in Mali has resulted in production remaining below expectations, requiring an update to the company's guidance,' citing supply-chain interruptions, delayed imports of critical mining inputs, inconsistent explosives supply during the wet season, and slower-than-anticipated mobilization of open-pit mining equipment at the A21 pit. Management continues to frame H2 2026 priorities around operational recovery at Syama, advancing Doropo construction, exploration, and financial discipline, underpinned by a strong net cash position that management says provides flexibility to fund growth without heavy reliance on new capital.

bull_case: Record and rising gold prices (spot has traded above $4,000-5,500/oz through 2026, with bank forecasts extending toward $5,000-6,000/oz) are driving outsized realized-price gains that are currently more than offsetting production shortfalls - H1 2026 net profit after tax rose to $162.6 million despite a ~31% YoY production decline

Strong, growing balance sheet with net cash of $317.4 million at 30 June 2026 (up 189% YoY) gives Resolute capacity to self-fund Doropo construction and withstand near-term operational setbacks without dilutive capital raises

Doropo brings genuine geographic diversification into a lower-risk jurisdiction (Côte d'Ivoire), reducing long-run dependence on Mali and supporting a credible path to a 500,000 oz/year run-rate by 2028

Large resource base (17.6 Moz global Mineral Resource) and continued exploration success (ABC Project upgraded to ~3.0 Moz Inferred) provide optionality well beyond current reserves, and the stock's consensus analyst rating is Buy with meaningful implied upside to price targets

Post-2024 crisis, management has rebuilt relationships with the Malian government (settlement concluded, ongoing 'constructive dialogue') and demonstrated the company can navigate extreme jurisdictional stress without losing operational control of its assets
bear_case: Syama concentration and West African/Sahel jurisdictional risk remain the central problem: the September 2026 guidance cut (group production down ~18% at the midpoint, AISC up ~12.5%) shows operational and security risk in Mali is recurring, not a one-off, and Barrick's parallel troubles in Mali underscore this is a sector-wide regional risk

Rising AISC (guided to $2,250-2,350/oz for FY2026, versus ~$1,650-1,750/oz as recently as 2025 guidance) show Resolute lacks a durable cost advantage; margin is increasingly dependent on the gold price staying elevated rather than internal cost discipline

Single-commodity, no-hedge-disclosed revenue model leaves the company fully exposed if gold prices retreat from current record levels (gold has already shown volatility in 2026, dipping below $4,000/oz in June after topping $5,500/oz in January)

Doropo execution risk is real and near-term: construction is capital intensive, with $105 million of local bank financing still to be finalized in Q3 2026, and first gold is not expected until H1 2028, leaving a multi-year gap before diversification benefits materialize

Guinea permit revocations and the unresolved Mali 2023 Mining Code implementation terms show regulatory risk in Resolute's operating jurisdictions is ongoing and unresolved, not fully priced-in or settled by the 2024 Protocol
